1: # VEPU510 H.264 encoder
2: 
3: The driver encodes one picture at a time and predicts each picture from the
4: reconstruction of the picture before it.  What that is worth, and how long a
5: group of pictures it is worth doing it over, was measured rather than assumed;
6: this file records the measurement.
7: 
8: ## Group length
9: 
10: A group is one IDR followed by pictures that predict from it and from each
11: other, so its length is what decides how much of a stream is the expensive
12: kind.  Two questions get two answers here: the driver's default is two
13: pictures (`RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_GOP`) and the streaming application asks for
14: fifteen (`CAMENC_DEFAULT_GOP`).  The driver does not know how its stream is
15: consumed, so it takes the shortest group that predicts at all; the
16: application does know, so it takes the group that is worth having and pays for
17: it knowingly.
18: 
19: ### Measured after the fault was fixed
20: 
21: This is the number to use.  1296x960 at quantiser 26, thirty frames a second,
22: on a source the encoder is asked to draw itself -- one constant background
23: with a small square moving slowly round it -- over 597 pictures.  Payload
24: bytes, so the container is not counted:
25: 
26: | pictures per group | IDR | P | payload | rate |
27: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
28: | 2 | 299 at 31350 B | 298 at 253 B | 9449442 B | 3799 kbit/s |
29: | 4 | 150 at 31368 B | 447 at 248 B | 4816531 B | **1937 kbit/s** |
30: 
31: Doubling the group halves the rate -- four is 51.0% of two -- and where the
32: bytes are says why.  Half the groups at two open with an IDR; a quarter of
33: them at four do.  Nothing else stands out, because a P is under one per cent
34: of an IDR and no P differs much from its neighbours:
35: 
36: | position in the group | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
37: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
38: | mean bytes | 31368 | 256 | 238 | 250 |
39: 
40: The quality is not what is being spent.  Decoding both streams and comparing
41: every picture with the source gives an RMSE of 0.78, and it is 0.78 for the
42: IDR and for each of the three P positions of a four-picture group: nothing
43: accumulates through the group.
44: 
45: Two numbers are enough to say what a longer group would do, because the rate
46: is `fps * 8 * (IDR/G + P)`: 3824 and 1942 kbit/s for two and four against the
47: 3799 and 1937 measured, and 561 for fifteen.  What that also says is where
48: the model stops being the answer.  The only term that falls with the group is
49: the IDR's, and it falls as 1/G, so the rate keeps improving -- but the price
50: of a long group is not in the rate.  A decoder that joined late, or that
51: missed a fragment, has to wait for the next picture a stream may start on,
52: which is one group away, and a fragment missed is not one picture lost but
53: everything up to that next start.
54: 
55: Fifteen is where those meet for a stream watched live: half a second at
56: thirty frames a second, which is a hiccup and not a wait, and far enough along
57: the curve that the rate is already a thirteenth of all-intra's.  Doubling it
58: again would take another 251 kbit/s off and add another half second to every
59: client's wait -- which is the trade, stated in the numbers it is made in.
60: 
61: ### Measured before it was fixed, which is what the fault looked like
62: 
63: The same measurement was taken on a 640x480 capture of a static scene -- a
64: ceiling light, no motion in frame, 60 frames, quantiser 26, no rate control --
65: while the encoder carried the fault described below.  It said a long group was
66: not worth having:
67: 
68: | pictures per group | IDR | P | payload | rate | against all-intra |
69: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
70: | 1 (all intra) | 60 | 0 | 186680 B | 1454 kbit/s | -- |
71: | 2 | 30 | 30 | 95862 B | 747 kbit/s | **-48.7%** |
72: | 4 | 15 | 45 | 90487 B | 705 kbit/s | -51.5% |
73: 
74: The all-intra row is not a capture.  It is the IDR mean of the other two
75: multiplied by 60, which is sound because the IDR mean is the same at both
76: group lengths to within 0.03% (3111 B against 3110 B) -- the cost of an IDR
77: does not depend on what surrounds it.
78: 
79: **Two was where the saving was.**  Going from one picture per group to two
80: took 48.7% off the rate, and it all came from the P pictures: a P was 84 bytes
81: where an IDR was 3111, which is 2.7%.
82: 
83: **Four was not.**  Doubling the group again halved the number of IDRs and
84: bought 5.6%.  The per-frame sizes said why:
85: 
86: ```
87: I 3010   p 100   p 3384   p  14
88: I 3006   p  12   p 3380   p  12
89: I 3014   p   9   p 3370   p  16
90: ```
91: 
92: One P in every group cost as much as the IDR that opened it -- 3380 bytes
93: against 3010 -- and those frames were worth 42415 of the 47830 bytes that
94: doubling the group saved.  Had they been as cheap as the P pictures at two per
95: group, four per group would have come out at 374 kbit/s; instead it came out
96: at 705.
97: 
98: Nothing was wrong with the streams, which is what made this look like a
99: property of the content: decoding both captures and comparing them frame for
100: frame gave an RMSE of about 1.1 out of 255 for every frame after the first
101: two, and within a group the reconstruction never got more than 1.2 RMSE away
102: from the IDR that opened it.
103: 
104: **The expensive P was the fault.**  It is explained now.  The register layer
105: programmed the anti-smear stage from the previous picture's state, which is
106: what the newer vendor code does and what the 1.0.6 library this driver was
107: measured against does not; with that state in force, a picture predicted from
108: a reference with its own local mean taken out of it.  The residual that leaves
109: is wrong, so the rate-distortion decision finds prediction not worth taking
110: and codes those pictures almost as intra -- which is exactly a P that costs
111: what an IDR costs, on content whose P pictures are otherwise nearly free.
112: Writing the 1.0.6 constants instead made both symptoms go: the pictures, which
113: had been drifting by the reference's own mean, and the rate.  The change is in
114: the driver's history.  A note on `rk3576_vepu_selftest_sequence()`, in
115: `rk3576_vepu.c`, describes a synthetic source on which the same thing used to
116: happen far more severely; that source is pathological -- a hard vertical edge
117: walking across the frame -- and is close to the worst input a predictive
118: encoder can be given.  It is kept as a canary, not as evidence about a scene.
119: 
120: Both tables are kept because they are the two halves of one lesson: a fault in
121: the prediction of P pictures shows up as a rate as much as as a picture, and
122: the rate finding was read as a fact about the content for as long as the
123: picture finding was read as a separate bug.
124: 
125: ## Upstream
126: 
127: Rockchip's own answer, in `rockchip-linux/mpp` issue #211 ("1080@30fps in
128: 2 Mbps encoding has ghosting"), was that the encoder has a strong preference
129: for coding skip pictures and that the resulting artefacts are not something MPP
130: is responsible for -- the reporter was told to raise it on their redmine
131: instead, with their FAE.  The same "a skip picture cannot be a reference"
132: mechanism is visible in MPP's source: it carries a `force_pskip_is_ref` option
133: in both its H.264 and its H.265 encoder, and its H.265 decoder picture buffer
134: has a comment about holding a reference buffer as a skip picture's
135: reconstruction buffer.  That option is off by default.  Issue #961, on this
136: same silicon with a long group, is open and unresolved.
137: 
138: None of this is a workaround, and none of it is what this driver had: the
139: fault above was in the state the driver programmed, not in the silicon's
140: handling of skip pictures.  It is kept here because a long group is what makes
141: the question worth asking -- issue #961 is a report of horizontal bars from
142: this encoder, on this silicon, with a long group, and it is unresolved.
143: 
144: ## The self-test
145: 
146: `rk3576_vepu_selftest()` runs at boot when `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST` is
147: set, and is the reason several of the above claims are checkable rather than
148: asserted.  It has two halves, and it runs the sequence test first because what
149: that test observes is the state before any picture has been encoded -- no
150: reference to predict from.
151: 
152:   * The **sequence test** encodes a moving source as an IDR followed by P
153:     pictures and checks that a P comes out cheaper than its own reference.
154:     Failing that check means prediction has stopped working, which is the
155:     failure that is otherwise silent: the stream still decodes, it is just at
156:     the wrong rate.
157:   * The **picture test** encodes static, gradient and noise sources and checks
158:     that the sizes come out in the order the sources' complexity implies, and
159:     that a NAL ends where the encoder said it did.
160: 
161: `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP` adds a hex dump of the coded stream, which is
162: not on by default because it is for reading with a decoder rather than from a
163: terminal.
164: 
165: ## What it prints at boot
166: 
167: Five lines, and nothing else:
168: 
169: ```
170: VEPU0: aclk=... hclk=... core=... (targets ... and ...)
171: VEPU0: VEPU510 rev ..., ip_id 0x..., h264=... hevc=... bframe=... fbc=..., res=..., osd=..., filter=...
172: VEPU0 sequence test: N frames, N bytes: IDR N B mean, P N B mean (N% of an IDR)
173: VEPU0 self-test: N frames, N bytes of bitstream, solid L/s, gradient L/s, noise L/s
174: VEPU0 codec self-test: N frames through the device node, N bytes of bitstream
175: ```
176: 
177: They report the two facts worth having at every boot -- which IP answered,
178: and whether the encode path works -- once for each layer that can break
179: independently: the hardware, the encode path, and the device node an
180: application actually talks to.  The clock rates are there because a core
181: clock left on its reset source makes the encoder work at a fraction of its
182: speed and say nothing about it.
183: 
184: The sequence test's line is the one to read if a stream is larger than it
185: should be: it reports the mean P picture against the mean IDR, and a P that
186: is not a small fraction of an IDR means prediction has stopped being used,
187: which is a failure that decodes correctly and only shows as size.
188: 
189: Everything else the driver knows -- which clock source each branch settled
190: on, what the dividers hold, the size of the reconstruction sets, a
191: frame-by-frame account of both self-tests -- goes through `vinfo()`, which
192: NuttX enables with `CONFIG_DEBUG_VIDEO_INFO` (its video subsystem debug
193: switch, off by default).  The detail is kept rather than deleted, so that it
194: can be asked for; it just is not printed twenty-odd lines at a time in front
195: of whatever does deserve attention.
196: 
197: Errors are not affected: `_err` is reported whatever the debug options say,
198: and `rk3576_vepu_dump()` prints the registers when an encode fails.
199:

# Nyabula · 星喵

### 基于 openvela 的 RK3576 桌面 AI 陪伴猫

**2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛 · 队伍 062 · Pharos Tech**

参赛方向：**新硬件适配 + AI 硬件产品创新**

Nyabula 是一只用双圆屏表达情绪、能听懂指令并执行设备动作的桌面陪伴猫。我们从 KICKPI-K7 的第一行串口输出开始，把 openvela 移植到 RK3576，逐步完成存储、原生 WiFi/蓝牙、音频、USB、双屏、启动恢复和产品运行时，最终打通 **唤醒 → 语音识别 → Agent → 工具执行或回答 → 语音合成 → 扬声器播报** 的完整交互回合。

设备可以使用 RK3576 NPU 上的本地 MiniCPM5-1B，也已接通小米 MiMo 在线 Agent。**openvela 负责产品状态、权限、工具执行、记忆、联网、存储、双眼和音频；Linux 通过 AMP 提供模型与摄像头计算服务。** 我们同时把开发过程沉淀为 24 份工程 Skill、构建与调试工具、可追溯的 PR 和 AI Coding 日志，希望交付一只可演示的猫，也交付一套其他团队能够继续使用的移植方法。

> **版本口径：2026-09-20，UTC+8。** 本文覆盖团队已完成的主线、产品分支和独立实验成果，并分别标明证据范围。完整语音功能由当日现场验收确认；产品集成在 [PR #93][p93]，尚未合入。24 份工程 Skill、双方 AI 日志与示例清理已分别经 [#95][p95]、[#96][p96]、[#98][p98]、[#97][p97] 合入。本文不是某一个最终镜像的全功能长稳认证。

**快速入口：** [作品亮点](#作品亮点) · [产品体验](#产品体验) · [架构](#系统架构) · [硬件与BSP](#硬件平台与-bsp) · [语音与Agent](#完整语音与双后端-agent) · [实测数据](#实测数据与验证范围) · [构建运行](#获取构建与运行) · [24份Skill](#24-份可复用工程-skill) · [交付状态](#交付状态与下一步)

## 作品亮点

| 亮点 | 我们完成了什么 | 为什么有价值 |
|---|---|---|
| 新 ARM64 平台适配 | 以 RK3399 移植为参考，完成 RK3576 的启动、GICv2、MMU、时钟、SMP/AMP 与外设适配 | 将高性能 Rockchip 平台接入 openvela，留下芯片层、板级层与设备驱动的清晰边界 |
| 原生无线 | SV6621/SWT6621S FullMAC WiFi 和 SDIO 蓝牙 transport；STA、SoftAP、WPA3 等独立板测 | openvela 自己持有无线与网络能力，计算域无需代管 WiFi |
| 完整语音产品链 | 本地唤醒、ASR、Agent、工具执行、TTS 和播报贯通；支持端侧与在线模型后端 | 从“模型能运行”推进到“设备能回应、能做事” |
| 异构协作 | 4×A53 openvela + 4×A72 Linux 拓扑、RPMsg、共享内存、模型按需传递 | 保留 openvela 的产品控制权，同时利用 RK3576 NPU 与 Linux 模型生态 |
| 可维护的设备 | N-Boot、NuttX/AMP 双域 A/B、摘要校验、Fastboot、运行态 nbootctl、面板 OTA | 从拔卡烧写演进为可持续开发、部署与恢复的设备 |
| 双眼与产品运行时 | 双 GC9B72 圆屏、Eye Engine、权限 Broker、JS/Wasm 插件、原生产品服务和自托管面板 | 把表情、状态、工具和交互统一到一个设备运行时 |
| AI 开发方法可复用 | 24 份工程 Skill；源码、反例、验证脚本、来源与边界一起交付 | 将一次比赛中的探索变成下一块板、下一个驱动可复用的工程知识 |

## 产品体验

### 已贯通的交互主线

1. **连接设备。** 通过设备 SoftAP 配网、二维码入口和浏览器控制台完成联网与设置。控制台由设备自身托管，HTTP 与 WebSocket 共享服务端口。
2. **看见反馈。** 双眼显示表情、凝视、眨眼、字幕和状态场景，语音回合中的聆听、处理与播报有对应视觉状态。
3. **自然说话。** 唤醒后采集语音、识别文本，交给同一个 Nyabot/官方 `ai_agent` 工具执行链；回复合成为声音并播放。赛事唤醒词遵循“你好，openvela / Hello, openvela”的要求。
4. **执行真实动作。** 已测的端侧指令包括读取时间、显示开心表情、创建五分钟计时器、设置或相对调整音量、写入长期记忆、建立闹钟与待办。设备状态实际变化，并返回 `sideEffectApplied:true`。
5. **选择模型后端。** 本地 MiniCPM5-1B 负责端侧回答与受约束的设备意图处理；在线 MiMo 已完成 HTTPS 调用和多工具成功回合。两类后端使用产品侧的权限和工具机制。
6. **持续维护。** 面板可管理设置、模型与升级；AMP 运行期间已经实测上传新固件、写非运行 AMP 槽、重启与确认。

以上语音主链、端侧工具动作、在线 Agent、面板和 OTA 各有当日功能验证；没有将其扩张成所有后端、异常、打断和并发组合均已完成测试。

### 使用场景与产品方向

Nyabula 面向桌面工作、学习与日常陪伴：用眼睛提供轻量反馈，用语音完成计时、提醒和设备控制，用可扩展工具连接其他服务。端侧模型为本地交互提供基础，在线模型扩展复杂语言处理能力。插件、MCP 和工程 Skill 则让设备具备继续扩展的空间。

当前定位是具有完整交互主线的工程原型。面向开发者的 openvela/Rockchip 参考平台与可扩展陪伴终端，是两条可继续探索的产品方向；成本、续航、量产结构和商业定价尚未完成验证。

for arg in "$@"; do

        --force|-f) FORCE=1 ;;
        --verify)  VERIFY=1 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,22p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "unknown option: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

[ -f "$MANIFEST" ] || { echo "ERROR: missing $MANIFEST" >&2; exit 1; }
NEXPECT=$(grep -c . "$MANIFEST")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- verify ----
verify() {
    local fail=0
    echo "=== 1. manifest vs on-disk ==="
    local missing=0 extra=0
    while read -r f; do
        [ -n "$f" ] || continue
        [ -s "$DEST/$f" ] || { echo "  MISSING: $f"; missing=$((missing+1)); }
    done < "$MANIFEST"
    # Only the vendored upstream files are tracked; the tooling and its build
    # artefacts live here too and are not part of the manifest.
    while read -r f; do

## port_regmodel.py —— VEPU510 寄存器模型移植工具

把这里的 VEPU510 寄存器**位域结构**移植成
`contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/hardware/rk3576_vepu510_reg.h`。

**为什么要用脚本而不是手工誊写**：寄存器模型约 3000 行 C 位域。手工誊写慢，更糟的是
**一处位宽写错会完全不可见** —— 它会让该寄存器所在的整个 32 位字都错，硬件只是行为
微妙地不对。机械变换可审计、可重复。

```bash
./port_regmodel.py            # 生成头文件（并内嵌编译期布局断言）
./port_regmodel.py --dump     # 显示每个定义的 keep/skip 决策
./port_regmodel.py --check    # 校验每个寄存器组的位宽和 == 32
./port_regmodel.py --compare  # ★ 用主机 gcc 同时编译「移植版」和「上游版」，
                              #   逐项 diff 所有 sizeof / offsetof
```

### 验证结果（2026-10-01）

```
checked 240 register groups (1 union groups not summable, skipped)
OK: every register group accounts for exactly 32 bits
OK: 463 sizeof/offsetof facts identical
```

- **463 项 sizeof/offsetof 与上游完全一致** —— 这是最强的验证：两边描述同一块硬件，
  任何位宽、成员顺序、缺失成员的错误都会暴露。
  上游头文件能在主机上编译（除去 MPP 辅助宏后它们是纯 typedef），
  所以不需要目标工具链就能对拍。
- 另有 22 条断言**内嵌进生成的头文件**（`_Static_assert(sizeof(X) == N, ...)`），
  这样以后任何编辑或换版本重新生成导致的布局变化都会**直接编译失败**，
  而不会静默改变写进编码器的寄存器内容。已用 aarch64 工具链验证通过。

### 有意的取舍

| 项 | 处理 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| `VepuFmtCfg` / `Vepu5xxOsdCfg` / `VepuRgb2YuvCfg` / `Vepu510NpuOut` | **不移植** | 体内含指针 / `Mpp*` 类型，是 MPP API 而非寄存器布局 |
| `VepuFmt` 等枚举 | **保留** | 其枚举值正是要写进格式寄存器的编码 |
| `Vepu510Dbg`（850 行） | 保留 | 正常路径不写它（只 debug 读回）；保留以求布局完整、零裁剪风险 |
| 上游的 `0x00000270 reg156` 注释 | 保留 | 把每个结构锚定到寄存器地址，是布局可校验的前提 |

### 一个值得知道的既成事实

上游 `Vepu510ControlCfg` 只有 **96 字节 = reg0..reg23**，而它的块注释写的是
`reg0 - reg72`（292 字节）。也就是说 **CTL 窗口的 reg24..reg155 从未被 MPP 写过**
（`H264eVepu510Sqi` 同理只覆盖 SQI 块的一部分）。这不是移植错误 —— 463 项对拍已证明
移植版与上游逐位一致 —— 而是 MPP 自身的模型：它只写它建模的那部分，其余靠
「写基础结构 + 多偏移补丁」的方式绕过。既然 MPP 是 Linux 上跑通的参考，
Phase 2b 就照它的写法定。但**如果编码器行为异常，reg24 以上是一个值得回头看的地方**。

## verify_regs.py —— 寄存器「取值」验证（对拍 MPP 的真实函数）

`contest2026_062_PharosTech/chips/rk3576/rk3576_vepu510_regs.{h,c}` 决定往寄存器里
**写什么值**。一个魔数写错会一直到"编码结果微妙地不对"才暴露，所以光读懂 MPP 不够 ——
必须对拍。

```bash
./verify_regs.py            # 构建并运行对拍
```

做法：MPP 的 `setup_vepu510_normal()` / `setup_vepu510_prep()` 是配置结构的纯函数，
而 MPP 头文件在主机上能编译。于是脚本按**花括号配对逐字提取**这两个函数的原文
（重命名以避免冲突），和我们自己实现的版本并排编译，对一组几何/格式跑两边，
**逐字节比较**得到的寄存器内容。

因为寄存器布局已先被证明与 MPP 一致（`port_regmodel.py --compare`，463 项），
所以直接比较两个结构体的字节是有效的端到端检查：如果我们多碰了一个字段、或漏了一个，
字节就会不同。

覆盖的用例：640x480 / 1280x720 / 1920x1080、带填充的 stride、非 16 倍对齐的
641x481 与 639x479、最小 16x16 与 17x17、以及
YUV420SP / YUV420SP_VU / YUV420P / YUV422SP / YUV422P / YUV422_YUYV / YUV400。

结果（2026-10-01）：
```
OK: control block and source-format block identical to MPP
```

**这个对拍当场抓到一个真 bug**：`MPP_FMT_YUV420SP_VU`（NV21）需要 `rbuv_swap = 1`，
而我一开始把它硬编码成 0。半平面格式的硬件 format code 对 NV12/NV21 是**同一个值**，
`rbuv_swap` 是唯一区分二者的位 —— 这正是最容易漏的那类错误。

**覆盖边界（诚实说明）**：
- `rbuv_swap` 由调用方给出（取自 MPP 的格式表），所以这里验证的是"该位写得对"，
  而不是"调用方推导得对"。
- **未覆盖**：本模块尚未实现的 codec / 率控 / AQ / 抗锯齿块；
  以及 MPP 从 fd 和运行时对象决定的缓冲区寻址（MPP 走 multi-offset ioctl，
  不写进结构体）。

framework's format table, so the RAW sensor data is demosaiced on
		the CPU inside this driver and the framework is presented with the
		finished NV12/YUV420 frame.  That keeps the frame buffer written by
		DMA and the buffer handed to the framework separate, and it avoids
		having to extend the shared format tables.

config RK3576_VEPU
	bool "Video Encoder (VEPU510)"
	default n
	---help---
		Enable the RK3576 hardware video encoder (VEPU510 at 0x27a00000),
		which implements H.264/H.265 and JPEG encoding.  Only the H.264
		fixed-QP path is driven so far.

		This provides power-domain, reset and clock bring-up, the
		register layer that programs an encode, the job layer that runs
		one on the hardware, and a V4L2 mem-to-mem device that presents
		the result to applications.

		The probe validates the whole power/clock/reset path in one step by
		reading the VEPU510 version register, which cannot answer until
		PD_VEPU0 is out of its memory-repair initial reset and its register
		bus is clocked -- so a version read is a genuine end-to-end check
		rather than a smoke test.

if RK3576_VEPU

config RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST
        bool "Encode synthetic pictures at boot"
        default y
        ---help---
                At boot, hand the encoder pictures built in memory and log what
                comes back: the bitstream length, the distortion figure, the
                interrupt status, and how many macroblocks were coded intra.

                This is the acceptance test for the encode path itself, the way the
                version probe is for the clocks and resets. The pictures are
                synthesised rather than captured, so a failure cannot be the
                camera's fault, and the configuration is the plainest one the
                register layer supports, so it cannot be a syntax bug either.

                There are two halves. One encodes a still picture three ways and
                checks the sizes come back in the order their complexity implies.
                The other encodes a moving sequence as one IDR followed by P
                pictures and checks that predicting costs less than not predicting
                -- a failure that is otherwise silent, because a stream whose
                prediction has stopped working still decodes, just at the wrong
                rate. See chips/rk3576/vepu/README.md.

                It costs about a megabyte of the DMA heap for the duration of the
                test, which is released as soon as the result is logged. Turn it off
                once the path is known good.

config RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP
        bool "Log the sequence test's bitstream in hex at boot"
        default n
        depends on RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST
        ---help---
                Log the whole of the sequence test's output as hex, one line per 64
                bytes, so it can be read back on a host with a decoder rather than
                from a terminal. rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_decode.py consumes it.

                Off by default: it is a few hundred lines of log for one picture,
                and what it is for is comparing the encoder's own picture against a
                host decoder's, which is a bring-up activity rather than a boot one.

endif # RK3576_VEPU

config RK3576_VEPU_CODEC
        bool "V4L2 memory-to-memory encoder device"
        default n
        depends on RK3576_VEPU
        depends on VIDEO_STREAM
        select SCHED_WORKQUEUE
        select SCHED_HPWORK
        ---help---
                Present the encoder as a /dev/videoN node that takes NV12 frames
                on its output side and returns an H.264 elementary stream on its
                capture side, using the V4L2 mem-to-mem framework.

                The output is annex-B and the stream's first frame carries the
                sequence and picture parameter sets in front of it, so what comes
                out of the device can be written to a file and played directly.

                A job is started by the queue operation that submits it and
                finished by the hardware's interrupt, so the bitstream is waited
                for with poll() on the device rather than by the queue operation
                blocking.  The completion runs on the high-priority work queue.

                This is a fixed-QP encoder. There is no rate control, and the frame
                rate only reaches the bitstream as VUI timing. Pictures are grouped,
                and all but the first of a group predict from the picture before
                them; see RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_GOP for the group length and why it is
                what it is.

if RK3576_VEPU_CODEC

config RK3576_VEPU_CODEC_SELFTEST
        bool "Run the encoder through its own V4L2 interface at boot"
        default y
        ---help---
                At boot, open the encoder's device node and drive it the way an
                application has to: negotiate both formats, request and map
                buffers, stream, and check the bitstream that comes back.

                This is the counterpart of RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST one layer up.
                That one proves the hardware encodes a frame; this one proves an
                application can reach it, which is a different claim. The three
                frames it encodes have different amounts of detail in them, so
                the sizes coming back in the right order is what says the encoder
                is responding to the picture.

endif # RK3576_VEPU_CODEC

########## h264_syntax.c
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 VEPU510 H.264 parameter set generation.
 *
 * The bit writer below is a reimplementation of the one Rockchip MPP uses
 * (mpp/base/mpp_bitwrite.c, Apache-2.0).  It is reproduced rather than
 * linked so that the driver does not drag an MPP internal into the kernel
 * build, and it is verified against MPP by byte comparison -- see
 * rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_sps_pps.py.
 *
 * Two behaviours in there are worth calling out because they are easy to get
 * wrong and impossible to notice by reading the output:
 *
 *   1. emulation prevention.  When two consecutive zero bytes have already
 *      been emitted and the next byte is below four, a 0x03 is inserted.
 *      The start code and the NAL header are written with the *raw* writer
 *      so that the leading 00 00 00 01 cannot itself be escaped, and so that
 *      the zero-byte run counter still reads zero when the RBSP begins.
 *
 *   2. mpp_writer_bytes() returns byte_cnt plus a pending partial byte, so a
 *      writer that has just emitted trailing bits reports a whole number.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

#include <nuttx/config.h>

#include <errno.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "h264_syntax.h"

/****************************************************************************
 * Private Types
 ****************************************************************************/

/* Bit writer state.  Field-for-field the same as MPP's MppWriteCtx, minus
 * the SEI-specific emulation counter which parameter sets never need.
 */

struct rk3576_h264_bw_s
{
  uint8_t *buffer;        /* first byte of the destination */
  uint8_t *stream;        /* next byte to fill             */
  uint32_t size;          /* destination capacity          */
  uint32_t byte_cnt;      /* whole bytes emitted           */
  uint32_t byte_buffer;   /* partially filled byte, left aligned */
  uint32_t buffered_bits; /* valid bits in byte_buffer, 0..7 */
  uint32_t zero_bytes;    /* trailing run of zero bytes    */
  bool overflow;
};

/* One row of MPP's level table (h264e_sps.c).  max_mbs is the largest frame
 * the level can carry, in macroblocks.
########## h264_syntax.h
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 VEPU510 H.264 parameter set generation.
 *
 * The VEPU510 *hardware* synthesizes the slice header from the synt_sli0/1/2
 * register fields.  Software therefore only has to supply the two parameter
 * sets that the hardware cannot produce on its own:
 *
 *   SPS   seq_parameter_set_rbsp()
 *   PPS   pic_parameter_set_rbsp()
 *
 * Both are emitted here with a start code prefix and RBSP trailing bits, so
 * the caller can concatenate
 *
 *   SPS | PPS | (hardware produced IDR slice)
 *
 * and get a decodable access unit.  Emulation prevention is applied to the
 * RBSP payload only, exactly as the H.264 spec requires and as Rockchip MPP
 * does it (mpp/base/mpp_bitwrite.c).
 *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Scope / supported configuration
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 *   - chroma_format_idc = 1 (4:2:0); 8-bit samples
 *   - frame_mbs_only_flag = 1 (progressive, no field coding)
 *   - num_slice_groups_minus1 = 0 (one slice group)
 *   - scaling lists are never transmitted
 *   - weighted prediction is off
 *
 * Profiles 66 (baseline), 77 (main) and 100 (high) are supported.  For
 * profile < 100 the PPS extension block (transform_8x8_mode_flag and
 * second_chroma_qp_index_offset) is omitted, matching MPP.
 *
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * How this is verified
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_sps_pps.py extracts MPP's h264e_sps_to_packet() and
 * h264e_pps_to_packet() verbatim, calls them, and compares the resulting
 * bytes against these functions over a matrix of geometries, levels and VUI
 * settings.  A single wrong bit anywhere (including in the emulation
 * prevention logic) shows up as a byte difference, so the whole writer is
 * covered, not just the parts that happen to be easy to reason about.
 *
 * The *policy* decisions that MPP makes in h264e_sps_update() -- level_idc
 * selection, log2_max_frame_num_minus4, cropping offsets -- are reproduced
 * here from that function's rules.  They are not byte-compared, because
 * h264e_sps_update() needs MPP's reference-configuration objects to run; the
 * rules are commented at each site instead.
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef __CHIPS_RK3576_VEPU_H264_SYNTAX_H
#define __CHIPS_RK3576_VEPU_H264_SYNTAX_H

/****************************************************************************
 * Included Files
 ****************************************************************************/

########## rk3576_vepu.c
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 VEPU0 (VEPU510 hardware video encoder) -- bring-up.
 *
 * This file currently does power, reset and clock bring-up plus a version
 * probe.  It owns no capture/codec state yet; the encoder driver is layered
 * on top.
 *
 * PD_VEPU0 has two traps worth repeating:
 *
 *   - Its memory-repair initial reset resets to 0, i.e. HELD IN RESET.  Until
 *     it is released, every VEPU0 register reads back as zero.
 *   - Its bus interface unit can be held idle independently of the clocks.
 *     A module in that state reads and writes registers perfectly while

/****************************************************************************
 * RK3576 VEPU510 as a V4L2 memory-to-memory video encoder.
 *
 * A job is started by the ioctl that queued it and finished by a work queue
 * item when the interrupt arrives.  It used to be encoded synchronously,
 * inside that ioctl, and the reason it is not any more is the application:
 * the wait is about 24 ms on a 1296x960 picture, and a program that is also
 * serving its sockets cannot spend that inside a queue operation.  The queue
 * operation now returns as soon as the encoder is running, and the frame is
 * published -- codec_capture_put_buf(), which is what moves the container
 * past vbuf_next and wakes a poller -- from the completion instead.
 *
 * That moves the job across two contexts, which is the whole of the cost: the
 * containers and the picture description have to live in the per-open state
 * between the halves, and the two contexts have to be kept out of each
 * other's way (priv->lock).  The split in rk3576_vepu.c between
 * rk3576_vepu_start() and rk3576_vepu_finish() is what makes the halves
 * possible; the hardware's own lock is held between them, so one job is in
 * the encoder at a time and the completion is what lets the next one in.
 *
 * Waiting for the bitstream is therefore the application's, and the device's
 * poll() is how it waits -- it is not a queue operation that blocks until a
 * frame is ready.

 * and this driver have to agree on them:

 *               drawn from by VIDIOC_QBUF
 *   vbuf_next   the container the driver is currently working on
 *
 * A queued container is not dequeueable until vbuf_next has moved past it,
 * which video_framebuff_capture_done() does.  So putting a frame in a
 * capture buffer and then calling codec_capture_put_buf() is what publishes
 * it; without that call the application would never see it, and calling it
 * before the data is in place would publish a half-written buffer.

这些驱动是 NuttX 的**内核级驱动**（lower-half driver），可以被使用相同方案、甚至不同
SoC 平台的多个板子复用（只要平台具备对应的外设总线下半边），因此源码收敛到本目录、
而非 `boards/` 下某个具体板子的目录。最终它们应当编入内核侧 `libdrivers.a`，与用户
程序（`libapps.a`）严格隔离。

## 目录层级架构

本目录（`contest2026_062_PharosTech/drivers`）通过**仓库内符号链接**

#define RK3576_VEPU_CID_QP                    \
  0x1000 /* 0..51, the QP every frame is      \
          * encoded at.  Fixed-QP is the only \
          * mode the register layer implements. */
#define RK3576_VEPU_CID_PROFILE                  \
  0x1001 /* 66, 77 or 100.  Lowering it below    \
          * 100 also drops the 8x8 transform and \
          * the second chroma offset, because    \
          * those are what the profile gates. */
#define RK3576_VEPU_CID_LEVEL            \
  0x1002 /* 0 lets the writer choose the \
          * smallest level the geometry fits. */
#define RK3576_VEPU_CID_DEBLOCK          \
  0x1003 /* 1 to carry deblocking filter \
          * control in the PPS. */
#define RK3576_VEPU_CID_GOP                              \
  0x1004 /* Pictures per group of pictures, 1..1000.     \
          * 1 makes every picture an IDR, which is what  \
          * the driver did before it could predict.  A   \
          * larger value makes the first picture of each \
          * group an IDR and the rest P pictures, which  \
          * is what makes the stream's bit rate depend   \
          * on the scene instead of only on the size of  \
          * the pictures. */

/* Frame rates are not controls: V4L2 already has a place for them, and
 * VIDIOC_S_PARM is where an application expects to set one.  The value
 * reaches the bitstream as the VUI timing block, so it tells a player how to
 * present the stream.  It does not govern how fast the encoder runs, because
 * nothing here is rate-controlled.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_QP      26
#define RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_PROFILE 66 /* baseline */
#define RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_LEVEL   0

/* Two pictures per group: one IDR and one P that predicts from it.
 *
 * This is the shortest group that predicts at all, and it is the driver's
 * default because the driver does not know how its stream is consumed.  A
 * group is also how long a decoder that arrived late has to wait before it can
 * start, so its length is a property of how a stream is watched rather than of
 * the encoding, and the caller is the one that can answer it.
 *
 * What the choice is worth is measured on this silicon in
 * chips/rk3576/vepu/README.md: two pictures per group is half the rate of one,
 * a longer group keeps paying, and a P picture is under one per cent of an
 * IDR.  The streaming application asks for fifteen, which is half a second at
 * its frame rate.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_GOP 2

/* The longest group a caller may ask for.  Not a hardware limit -- the limits
 * that matter are the widths of frame_num and pic_order_cnt_lsb in the slice
 * header, and those are far larger.  It is a limit on how long a stream can
 * go before a decoder that joined late has nothing to start from.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU_GOP_MAX 1000

 * only that the group be long compared with how many pictures an IDR is worth,

 * the diminishing returns are not: the rate keeps falling with the group,
 * because the term that falls is the IDR's, and it falls as 1/G.
 *
 * What stops being worth it is the other side of the same coin.  A group is

/* The status block's raw words, which the encoder writes when a job finishes.
 *
 * These are offsets into a register file rather than members of a struct
 * because neither figure worth reading fits in one register: the bitstream
 * length's top eight bits share a register with the distortion figure's low
 * half, and the distortion figure's high half is the next register along.
 * The modelled Vepu510Status has all of them, but as bitfields -- and a
 * bitfield has no offset, so there is nothing for a header to point at.
 *
 * The low half of the length is the whole of it here: a buffer large enough
 * to need the other eight bits would be 4 GB, which this driver cannot be
 * given.  MPP reads it the same way.
 *
 * What the split means for a reader is spelled out at
 * rk3576_vepu510_status_decode(), which is the only thing that should be
 * assembling these.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_BS_LGTH_OFFSET 0x4000
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_SSE_LOW_OFFSET 0x4004 /* sse_l16 in bits 31:16 */

/* The smear counts the encoder reports for the picture it just encoded, as
 * four eight-bit fields in one word.  This is the half of the status block
 * that feeds back into the *next* picture's registers -- see
 * rk3576_vepu510_status_smear() -- and it is read like the rest of the status
 * block, from task context after the job has finished.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_SMEAR_CNT_OFFSET 0x40a4

/* What one step of a smear count is worth.  The encoder counts in units of
 * four macroblocks, so the status field is a quarter of the count the
 * anti-smear thresholds are expressed in and MPP multiplies it back.
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_SMEAR_CNT_SCALE 4
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_SSE_HIGH_OFFSET 0x4008

/* How the picture was actually coded: the block counts the encoder reports
 * for the picture it just encoded, split by prediction mode and block size.
 *
 * This is the only place the choice between intra and inter coding of a
 * finished picture is visible.  A length says what the picture cost and a
 * distortion figure says how good it is, and neither distinguishes a picture
 * that predicted well from one that gave up and coded itself from the source
 * -- but the two have opposite causes, and a picture that costs an I
 * picture's worth of bits while claiming to be predicted is exactly the case
 * where that distinction is the whole question.  MPP reads the same fields
 * for its rate control (iblk4_prop is these counts over the macroblock
 * count).
 */

#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_QP_SUM_OFFSET   0x400c
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_PNUM_P16_OFFSET 0x4088
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_PNUM_P8_OFFSET  0x408c
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_PNUM_I32_OFFSET 0x4090
#define RK3576_VEPU510_ST_PNUM_I16_OFFSET 0x4094

*
 * Returned Value:
 *   OK on success.  A negated errno on failure: -ETIMEDOUT if the encoder
 *   never signalled completion, -EIO if it completed with an error bit set
 *   or produced no bitstream, -EINVAL for an unusable description.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int rk3576_vepu_encode(FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_frame_s *frm,
                       FAR const struct rk3576_h264_cfg_s *cfg,
                       FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_slice_s *slice,
                       FAR struct rk3576_vepu_result_s *result);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rk3576_vepu_start
 *
 * Description:
 *   The first half of rk3576_vepu_encode(): validate the description and hand
 *   the picture to the hardware, returning as soon as the encoder is running.
 *
 *   This exists for a caller that has something better to do than wait for
 *   the interrupt -- the codec driver's queue operation, which has to return
 *   to an application that is servicing more than the encoder.  Such a caller
 *   completes the job with rk3576_vepu_finish() when it learns the job is
 *   over, wherever that turns out to be.
 *
 *   **The mutex is held on return.**  The hardware runs one job at a time and
 *   the mutex is what says whose it is, so a successful start and its finish
 *   are one critical section: the lock is not released in between, and only
 *   rk3576_vepu_finish() may release it.  A caller that starts a job must
 *   therefore reach its finish, and must not block in between on anything
 *   that itself waits for the encoder.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   frm    - source picture, source buffer and destination buffer
 *   cfg    - H.264 syntax parameters
 *   slice  - slice-level values for this picture
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   OK with the mutex held and the job running.  A negated errno on failure,
 *   with no job started and the mutex released: -EINVAL for an unusable
 *   description, -ENODEV if the encoder is not up.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int rk3576_vepu_start(FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_frame_s *frm,
                      FAR const struct rk3576_h264_cfg_s *cfg,
                      FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_slice_s *slice);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rk3576_vepu_finish
 *
 * Description:
 *   The second half of rk3576_vepu_encode(): wait for the job
 *   rk3576_vepu_start() started, read what it reported, and release the mutex
 *   the start took.
 *
 *   frm and slice must be the same descriptions the start was given, because
 *   what the completion needs -- the destination to invalidate in the cache
 *   and the picture type to report feedback for -- is in them.
 *
 * Input Parameters:
 *   frm    - the same source picture and destination the start was given
 *   slice  - the same slice-level values the start was given
 *   result - receives what the encoder reported; may be NULL
 *
 * Returned Value:
 *   OK on success.  A negated errno on failure: -ETIMEDOUT if the encoder
 *   never signalled completion, -EIO if it completed with an error bit set or
 *   produced no bitstream.  Either way the mutex is released, and a failure
 *   also drops the reconstruction reference so that the next picture has to
 *   re-establish it.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

int rk3576_vepu_finish(FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_frame_s *frm,
                       FAR const struct rk3576_vepu510_slice_s *slice,
                       FAR struct rk3576_vepu_result_s *result);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: rk3576_vepu_dump
 *
 * Description:
 *   Log the encoder's state and the registers that decide whether it started
 *   at all.  Intended to be called when a job times out or reports an error,
 *   from task context.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

void rk3576_vepu_dump(void);

# RK3576 VEPU510 H.264 编码器驱动

本目录是 openvela / NuttX 上 RK3576 硬件视频编码器 **VEPU510** 的内核侧驱动。
VEPU510 位于 `0x27a00000`，在 `PD_VEPU0` 电源域内，IP 本身支持 H.264、H.265 和
JPEG 编码；本驱动目前只驱动 **H.264、固定 QP** 这一条路径，并把它呈现为一个
V4L2 mem-to-mem 设备节点：output 队列收 NV12 原始帧，capture 队列出 annex-B
H.264 码流。

板级入口在 `boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_boardinit.c`：先调用
`rk3576_vepu_initialize()` 完成电源、复位、时钟与版本探测，再调用
`rk3576_vepu_codec_register("/dev/video1")` 注册设备节点（`/dev/video0` 归 VICAP
摄像头）。参考应用是 `app/camenc`。

## 代码结构

| 文件 | 职责 | 编译开关 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rk3576_vepu.c` | 电源域 / 复位 / 时钟 bring-up、版本探测、一次编码的 start 与 finish、状态块解码、开机自检 | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU` |
| `rk3576_vepu.h` | 上述硬件层的公开接口 | 同上 |
| `vepu510_regs.c` / `.h` | 一帧该往寄存器里写什么值（控制块、源格式、地址、码流语法、固定 QP 率控块） | 同上 |
| `vepu510_tables.c` / `.h` | 寄存器层使用的 tuning 表：RDO lambda、anti-flicker 阈值与权重 | 同上 |
| `h264_syntax.c` / `.h` | SPS / PPS 生成与 RBSP bit writer；切片头由硬件从 `synt_sli0/1/2` 寄存器综合，软件不生成 | 同上 |
| `rk3576_vepu_codec.c` / `.h` | V4L2 M2M 设备节点、缓冲区与 streaming 状态机、作业调度 | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC` |
| `hardware/rk3576_vepu510_reg.h` | 寄存器布局模型（**生成文件**，勿手改；由 `rk3576-mpp-ref/port_regmodel.py` 重新生成） | 随 `rk3576_vepu.c` |

## 上电与探测次序

1. 释放 `PD_VEPU0` 的 memory-repair 初复位，并保持该电源域供电。**该复位是保持
   状态**，未释放前域内每个寄存器都读回 0——看起来就像驱动什么都没写。
2. 释放 CRU 软件复位。
3. 打开时钟，包括总线接口门控。`PD_VEPU0` 的 BIU 可以独立于时钟被挂起：这种
   状态下寄存器读写完全正常，却发不出一条 AXI 事务（`rk3576_vicap.c` 记录了
   `PD_VI` 上同样的陷阱）。
4. 读 VEPU510 版本寄存器并检查 `h264_cap`。这一步同时验证了电源、复位、时钟
   整条路径，是真正的端到端检查而不是冒烟测试。

时钟频率**不在这里设定**：寄存器访问只需要 `aclk`/`hclk`，core 时钟由驱动在能够
测量候选父时钟之后按设备树目标设置（ACLK 400 MHz、core 702 MHz，见
`hardware/rk3576_vepu.h`）。

## 应用接口

* **设备节点**：`/dev/video1`。
* **格式**：output 侧只接受 `V4L2_PIX_FMT_NV12`；capture 侧给出
  `V4L2_PIX_FMT_H264`，annex-B 封装，流的第一个访问单元前带 SPS 与 PPS，因此
  写进文件即可直接播放。
* **内存**：只接受 MMAP 缓冲区。
* **私有 control**：编号从 `0x1000` 起。它们必须是私有的，因为
  `v4l2_m2m.c` 的 `struct v4l2_ext_control` 把 `id` 声明为 `uint16_t`（标准是
  `uint32_t`），所有 `V4L2_CID_MPEG_*`（`0x009809xx` 以上）都不可达，
  `V4L2_CID_PRIVATE_BASE`（`0x08000000`）同样放不进这个字段；框架的
  `query_ext_ctrl` 未接通，所以应用无法枚举，必须使用下表编号。

  | CID | 名称 | 取值 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `0x1000` | QP | 0..51，每帧编码使用的量化参数 |
  | `0x1001` | profile | 66 / 77 / 100；低于 100 会同时去掉 8x8 变换和第二个色度 QP 偏移 |
  | `0x1002` | level | 0 表示由写入方选择几何尺寸所需的最小 level |
  | `0x1003` | deblock | 1 表示在 PPS 中携带去块滤波控制 |
  | `0x1004` | GOP | 每组图像数 1..1000；1 表示每帧都是 IDR，大于 1 时每组首帧为 IDR、其余为 P 帧 |

* **帧率**：不是 control，走 V4L2 已有的 `VIDIOC_S_PARM`。它只作为 VUI timing
  进入码流，告诉播放器如何呈现；本驱动没有码率控制，帧率不决定编码器跑多快。
* **等待模型**：`VIDIOC_QBUF` 提交作业后立即返回，作业在硬件中断（高优先级工作
  队列）上完成；应用用 `poll()` 等待码流，而不是让队列操作阻塞。
* **预测约束**：一组内非首帧不能单独丢弃——其后的图像从它预测，缺失的参考会让
  解码器把后续画面解错。需要丢帧的调用方应当改为让客户端从下一组重新开始
  （`app/camenc/camenc_ws.h` 中 `waiting` 的注释说明了这一约定）。

## Kconfig 选项

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU` | n | 驱动本体：电源/复位/时钟、寄存器层、作业层 |
| `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST` | y | 开机用内存中合成的图像跑编码路径验收测试 |
| `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP` | n | 把序列测试的码流以十六进制打进日志，供主机侧解码器读取 |
| `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC` | n | 注册 V4L2 M2M 设备节点 |
| `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC_SELFTEST` | y | 开机通过设备节点本身跑一遍完整的应用侧流程 |

## 开机输出与自检

打开驱动后开机固定打印五行：

```
VEPU0: aclk=... hclk=... core=... (targets ... and ...)
VEPU0: VEPU510 rev ..., ip_id 0x..., h264=... hevc=... bframe=... fbc=..., res=..., osd=..., filter=...
VEPU0 sequence test: N frames, N bytes: IDR N B mean, P N B mean (N% of an IDR)
VEPU0 self-test: N frames, N bytes of bitstream, solid L/s, gradient L/s, noise L/s
VEPU0 codec self-test: N frames through the device node, N bytes of bitstream
```

这五行报告每次开机都值得知道的两件事——**哪一颗 IP 应答了**、**编码路径是否
可用**——并且按可以独立损坏的层次各报一次：硬件、编码路径、应用实际面对的
设备节点。时钟频率之所以要打印，是因为 core 时钟若停在复位源上，编码器会以
几分之一的速度工作却什么都不说。

自检由此分两段：

* **序列测试**（`rk3576_vepu_selftest_sequence()`）把运动图像编成一个 IDR 加若干
  P 帧，检查 P 帧比它自己的参考帧更省。这一项失败意味着预测已经失效——这是
  一种无声的故障：码流照样能解码，只是码率不对。
* **图像测试**编码静止、渐变和噪声三种源，检查码流长度按源的复杂度排序，并检查
  NAL 在编码器声称的位置结束。

`CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC_SELFTEST` 是同一件事在设备节点层再做一遍：协商格式、
申请并映射缓冲区、streaming、检查回来的码流，证明应用确实能到达编码器。

出错信息不受调试开关影响：`_err` 始终输出，编码失败时 `rk3576_vepu_dump()` 会
打印寄存器。其余细节（每个时钟分支落在哪个源、分频值、重建集大小、两段自检
的逐帧记录）走 `vinfo()`，由 NuttX 的 `CONFIG_DEBUG_VIDEO_INFO` 打开，默认关闭。

## 主机侧验证

移植的正确性不靠阅读保证，而靠在主机上把我们的实现与上游 MPP 并排编译对拍。
脚本位于工作区的 `rk3576-mpp-ref/`（参考与验证目录，**不随本仓交付**）：

| 脚本 | 验证内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `port_regmodel.py --compare` | 生成头文件与上游逐项对拍 `sizeof`/`offsetof`（463 项一致），`--check` 校验每个寄存器组的位宽和恰为 32 位 |
| `verify_regs.py` | 提取 MPP 的 `setup_vepu510_normal()` / `setup_vepu510_prep()` 原文，与 `vepu510_regs.c` 逐字节比较寄存器内容 |
| `verify_sps_pps.py` | 与 MPP 的 `h264e_sps_to_packet()` / `h264e_pps_to_packet()` 逐字节比较 SPS/PPS |
| `verify_decode.py` | 读取 `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP` 输出的十六进制码流，用主机解码器复核 |

同一目录下的 `fetch.sh --verify` 可离线复核上游快照的清单完整性与许可证边界。

## 范围与限制

* **固定 QP**：没有码率控制、没有 AQ、没有 ROI；帧率只进 VUI。
* **无 B 帧**：硬件报告 `bframe=0`，一组就是「一个 IDR + 若干 P」。
* **只驱动 H.264**：HEVC、JPEG 编码和硬件解码能力都没有接入。
* **只支持 NV12 输入、H.264 输出**，4:2:0、8 bit、progressive（`frame_mbs_only`）。
* **硬件一次只跑一个作业**，由互斥量保证；`rk3576_vepu_start()` 成功返回时持有
  该互斥量，必须由 `rk3576_vepu_finish()` 释放，两者之间不得阻塞在同样等待
  编码器的东西上。

1: # RK3576 VEPU510 H.264 编码器驱动
2: 
3: 本目录是 openvela / NuttX 上 RK3576 硬件视频编码器 **VEPU510** 的内核侧驱动。
4: VEPU510 位于 `0x27a00000`，在 `PD_VEPU0` 电源域内，IP 本身支持 H.264、H.265 和
5: JPEG 编码；本驱动目前只驱动 **H.264、固定 QP** 这一条路径，并把它呈现为一个
6: V4L2 mem-to-mem 设备节点：output 队列收 NV12 原始帧，capture 队列出 annex-B
7: H.264 码流。
8: 
9: 板级入口在 `boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_boardinit.c`：先调用
10: `rk3576_vepu_initialize()` 完成电源、复位、时钟与版本探测，再调用
11: `rk3576_vepu_codec_register("/dev/video1")` 注册设备节点（`/dev/video0` 归 VICAP
12: 摄像头）。参考应用是 `app/camenc`。
13: 
14: ## 代码结构
15: 
16: | 文件 | 职责 | 编译开关 |
17: | --- | --- | --- |
18: | `rk3576_vepu.c` | 电源域 / 复位 / 时钟 bring-up、版本探测、一次编码的 start 与 finish、状态块解码、开机自检 | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU` |
19: | `rk3576_vepu.h` | 上述硬件层的公开接口 | 同上 |
20: | `vepu510_regs.c` / `.h` | 一帧该往寄存器里写什么值（控制块、源格式、地址、码流语法、固定 QP 率控块） | 同上 |
21: | `vepu510_tables.c` / `.h` | 寄存器层使用的 tuning 表：RDO lambda、anti-flicker 阈值与权重 | 同上 |
22: | `h264_syntax.c` / `.h` | SPS / PPS 生成与 RBSP bit writer；切片头由硬件从 `synt_sli0/1/2` 寄存器综合，软件不生成 | 同上 |
23: | `rk3576_vepu_codec.c` / `.h` | V4L2 M2M 设备节点、缓冲区与 streaming 状态机、作业调度 | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC` |
24: | `hardware/rk3576_vepu510_reg.h` | 寄存器布局模型（**生成文件**，勿手改；由 `rk3576-mpp-ref/port_regmodel.py` 重新生成） | 随 `rk3576_vepu.c` |
25: 
26: ## 上电与探测次序
27: 
28: 1. 释放 `PD_VEPU0` 的 memory-repair 初复位，并保持该电源域供电。**该复位是保持
29:    状态**，未释放前域内每个寄存器都读回 0——看起来就像驱动什么都没写。
30: 2. 释放 CRU 软件复位。
31: 3. 打开时钟，包括总线接口门控。`PD_VEPU0` 的 BIU 可以独立于时钟被挂起：这种
32:    状态下寄存器读写完全正常，却发不出一条 AXI 事务（`rk3576_vicap.c` 记录了
33:    `PD_VI` 上同样的陷阱）。
34: 4. 读 VEPU510 版本寄存器并检查 `h264_cap`。这一步同时验证了电源、复位、时钟
35:    整条路径，是真正的端到端检查而不是冒烟测试。
36: 
37: 时钟频率**不在这里设定**：寄存器访问只需要 `aclk`/`hclk`，core 时钟由驱动在能够
38: 测量候选父时钟之后按设备树目标设置（ACLK 400 MHz、core 702 MHz，见
39: `hardware/rk3576_vepu.h`）。
40: 
41: ## 应用接口
42: 
43: * **设备节点**：`/dev/video1`。
44: * **格式**：output 侧只接受 `V4L2_PIX_FMT_NV12`；capture 侧给出
45:   `V4L2_PIX_FMT_H264`，annex-B 封装，流的第一个访问单元前带 SPS 与 PPS，因此
46:   写进文件即可直接播放。
47: * **内存**：只接受 MMAP 缓冲区。
48: * **私有 control**：编号从 `0x1000` 起。它们必须是私有的，因为
49:   `v4l2_m2m.c` 的 `struct v4l2_ext_control` 把 `id` 声明为 `uint16_t`（标准是
50:   `uint32_t`），所有 `V4L2_CID_MPEG_*`（`0x009809xx` 以上）都不可达，
51:   `V4L2_CID_PRIVATE_BASE`（`0x08000000`）同样放不进这个字段；框架的
52:   `query_ext_ctrl` 未接通，所以应用无法枚举，必须使用下表编号。
53: 
54:   | CID | 名称 | 取值 |
55:   | --- | --- | --- |
56:   | `0x1000` | QP | 0..51，每帧编码使用的量化参数 |
57:   | `0x1001` | profile | 66 / 77 / 100；低于 100 会同时去掉 8x8 变换和第二个色度 QP 偏移 |
58:   | `0x1002` | level | 0 表示由写入方选择几何尺寸所需的最小 level |
59:   | `0x1003` | deblock | 1 表示在 PPS 中携带去块滤波控制 |
60:   | `0x1004` | GOP | 每组图像数 1..1000；1 表示每帧都是 IDR，大于 1 时每组首帧为 IDR、其余为 P 帧 |
61: 
62: * **帧率**：不是 control，走 V4L2 已有的 `VIDIOC_S_PARM`。它只作为 VUI timing
63:   进入码流，告诉播放器如何呈现；本驱动没有码率控制，帧率不决定编码器跑多快。
64: * **等待模型**：`VIDIOC_QBUF` 提交作业后立即返回，作业在硬件中断（高优先级工作
65:   队列）上完成；应用用 `poll()` 等待码流，而不是让队列操作阻塞。
66: * **预测约束**：一组内非首帧不能单独丢弃——其后的图像从它预测，缺失的参考会让
67:   解码器把后续画面解错。需要丢帧的调用方应当改为让客户端从下一组重新开始
68:   （`app/camenc/camenc_ws.h` 中 `waiting` 的注释说明了这一约定）。
69: 
70: ## Kconfig 选项
71: 
72: | 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
73: | --- | --- | --- |
74: | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU` | n | 驱动本体：电源/复位/时钟、寄存器层、作业层 |
75: | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST` | y | 开机用内存中合成的图像跑编码路径验收测试 |
76: | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SEQ_DUMP` | n | 把序列测试的码流以十六进制打进日志，供主机侧解码器读取 |
77: | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC` | n | 注册 V4L2 M2M 设备节点 |
78: | `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_CODEC_SELFTEST` | y | 开机通过设备节点本身跑一遍完整的应用侧流程 |
79:

## 调研结论：`apps/examples` 编译中间文件存放位置

openvela 有 **两套构建体系**，中间文件位置不同：

### 1. CMake 构建（默认，推荐）

通过 `lunch` + `m` 构建时，使用 **out-of-tree** CMake 构建。

**中间文件位置：**
```
<workspace>/out/<vendor>_<board>_<config>/apps/examples/<name>/CMakeFiles/...
```

例如 kickpi-k7 的 hello 示例：
```
cmake_out/kickpi-k7_nsh/apps/examples/hello/CMakeFiles/apps_hello.dir/hello_main.c.o
```

完整 BINARY 目录由 `lunch` 时确定，默认规则（见 `build/envsetup.sh` 第549行）：
```bash
CURRENT_LUNCH_BINARY_DIR=${TOP_DIR}/out/${vendor}_${board}_${config}
```

### 2. Makefile 构建（遗留模式）

标记为 makefile 的 config（通过 `add_makefile_choice`）走传统 NuttX Makefile 构建。这种情况下：

#### a) 默认情况（无 unionfs）
**中间文件就放在源码目录内**，与 `.c` 文件同级。由于 `PREFIX` 默认为空，`SUFFIX` 将路径中的 `/` 替换为 `.`：

从 `apps/Application.mk` 第 51、87-89 行：
```makefile
SUFFIX ?= $(subst $(DELIM),.,$(CWD))   # DELIM=/ → 路径变成用点连接
COBJS = $(CSRCS:%=$(PREFIX)%$(SUFFIX)$(OBJEXT))
```

以 `apps/examples/hello/hello_main.c` 为例，生成的 `.o` 文件名类似于：
```
hello_main.c.home.yunline.projects.ovela-dev-workspace.apps.examples.hello.o
```
就放在 `apps/examples/hello/` 目录下（`PREFIX` 为空时就是当前目录）。

#### b) unionfs overlay 模式（`build.sh`）
`build.sh` 使用 `unionfs-fuse` 创建 overlay 文件系统（copy-on-write）：
```bash
unionfs-fuse -o cow ${OUTDIR}=RW:${ROOTDIR}=RO ${MOUNTDIR}
```
此时源码目录为只读（RO），所有写入（包括 `.o` 文件）全部落到 `OUTDIR` 对应的 RW 层，所以在 unionfs 挂载的视角下中间文件看似在源目录，实际物理存储在 OUTDIR。

### 总结对照表

| 构建方式 | 中间文件 (.o) 位置 | 说明 |
|---------|-------------------|------|
| **CMake** (默认) | `out/<vendor>_<board>_<config>/apps/examples/.../CMakeFiles/...` | 完全 out-of-tree |
| **Makefile** (普通) | `apps/examples/<name>/` 自身目录下 | 文件名带 SUFFIX 后缀（路径用 `.` 连接） |
| **Makefile** (unionfs) | `OUTDIR` 指定的可写层目录 | 通过 overlay 实现写时复制，逻辑上在源码目录 |"}

# 从开启 NuttX trace 到可视化完整流程

## 第 1 步：在 `configs/display/defconfig` 中加入 trace 相关配置

需要在原来的 defconfig 里追加以下项（当前 display 场景**一个都没有**，需从零加）：

```kconfig

CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION=y
CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_FILTER=y
CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_SWITCH=y
CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_IRQHANDLER=y
CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_SYSCALL=y

CONFIG_DRIVERS_NOTE_TASKNAME_BUFSIZE=64
CONFIG_DRIVERS_NOTERAM=y
CONFIG_DRIVERS_NOTERAM_BUFSIZE=65536   # 环形缓冲，越大越能装更多事件

```

> 说明：
> - `CONFIG_SYSTEM_SYSTEM=y`（display/defconfig 已有）满足 `trace cmd` 依赖。
> - FLAT 构建下 `CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION_SYSCALL` 需 `--wrap` 链接器选项生效，openvela 构建系统一般已自动处理；若你只关心线程切换/IRQ，可暂不开 syscall 以减小开销。

## 第 2 步：重新配置 + 编译

```

./build.sh   # 或你们场景使用的构建脚本，重新跑 menuconfig/编译生成 nuttx.bin

```

## 第 3 步：在板子 NSH 上采集 trace

串口（COM4, 1500000 baud）进 NSH 后：

```
nsh> trace start           # 开始采集（可带秒数：trace start 10）
# ... 跑你的 nyabula demo ...
nsh> trace stop            # 停止
nsh> trace dump            # 把采集数据打印到串口
```

更省事的方式——「边跑某条命令边抓」：
```
nsh> trace cmd nyabula_display      # 运行该命令并同时抓取其 trace
nsh> trace dump /dev/sd0/trace.txt  # 或直接落到存储文件（如果板上有挂载的存储）

## 第 4 步：把 trace 数据弄到主机

两种方式：

1. **串口转储**：`trace dump` 会输出形如下面的 ftrace 文本，用串口工具的日志保存功能存成 `.txt`（这就是 Trace Compass 的输入）。示例：
   ```
   nyabula_te-5   [0]   7.640000000: sched_switch: prev_comm=... ==> next_comm=...
   nyabula_te-5   [0]   7.650000000: irq_handler_entry: irq=15
   ```
2. **文件落到存储**后，用 `adb pull`（你板子有 USB ADB）或 `ymodem`/`zmodem` 传到主机。

**方式 A —— Trace Compass（任务 trace 官方配套）**
1. 下载安装 [Eclipse Trace Compass](https://www.eclipse.org/tracecompass/)。
2. 打开后 `Tools → Add-ons` 安装扩展 **“Trace Compass ftrace (Incubation)”**（ftrace 格式解析器）。
3. `File → Open Trace`，选择第 4 步导出的 trace 文本文件。
4. 即可看到每线程的时间线（线程状态/切换/IRQ/syscall 事件）。

**方式 B —— Perfetto（更现代的选择）**

```

```
（这需要先从 `/dev/note` 拿到**二进制** note 记录而非 ftrace 文本；然后拖入 [ui.perfetto.dev](https://ui.perfetto.dev) 查看。）

- **`trace dump` 输出的其实是 ftrace 文本**，不是二进制 —— 直接喂给 Trace Compass 即可，不需要额外的 pynuttx 解析。pynuttx/Perfetto 那条路适合你想拿二进制 `/dev/note` 原始流时用。

1: # camenc: conversion to a non-blocking event loop — construction plan
2: 
3: Status: **planned, not started** (2026-10-05). Supersedes the four-thread model in
4: `camenc-refactor-state.md`; that file's scheduler analysis still stands, but the
5: threading is now off the table in favour of one non-blocking loop.
6: 
7: ## The decision
8: 
9: One thread, one `poll()`, an explicit state machine. Threading was dropped
10: because on a single core it reduces no work — it only moves it — while costing
11: priority tuning, mailboxes and quiesce handshakes that a loop does not need.
12: 
13: The wake primitive is `poll()`, **not** semaphores. There is no "wait on N
14: semaphores, wake on any" in POSIX, and none is needed: every wake source here is
15: already a file descriptor, and `poll()` is exactly that primitive. Verified:
16: 
17: | Fact | Evidence |
18: | --- | --- |
19: | A completed capture frame wakes poll | `capture_poll` in the fops (`v4l2_cap.c:359`); `poll_notify(..., POLLIN)` on completion (`:2024`) |
20: | A queued encoder capture buffer wakes poll | `codec_poll` in `g_codec_fops` (`v4l2_m2m.c:218`); `poll_notify` in the qbuf path (`:1175`) |
21: | A new connection wakes poll | `tcp_listen.c:297` posts `TCP_BACKLOG` → `tcp_netpoll.c:86` maps it to `POLLIN` |
22: | DQBUF can be non-blocking | `v4l2_cap.c:2406-2408`: with `O_NONBLOCK` and nothing ready it returns `-EAGAIN` |
23: | `accept()` will not block after poll says readable | the connection is already in the backlog: `tcp_accept.c:223-232` |
24: | A `poll()` timeout costs no CPU | `fs_poll.c:495` — `nxsem_tickwait(sem, MSEC2TICK(timeout))`, a plain semaphore sleep |
25: 
26: ⚠ A timeout is a **safety net, not a polling interval**. The camera wakes the
27: loop 30–60 times a second regardless, so the loop can never sit waiting on a
28: client that never connects.
29: 
30: ### The one gap poll cannot close
31: 
32: The loop is not always *in* `poll()`. The encoder's `QBUF` runs the job
33: synchronously inside the ioctl (`vepu_service()` → `rk3576_vepu_encode()`
34: → `nxsem_tickwait(&g_vepu_done, ...)` at `rk3576_vepu.c:1631`), which is 24 ms on
35: 1296x960 during which no socket is serviced. Closing that window is step (b).
36: 
37: ## Phase 0 — baseline
38: 
39: Capture `us/frame:` and the frame rate for the modes in use before touching
40: anything. Phase A claims to change no behaviour, and that claim needs a
41: before-picture to be checkable against.
42: 
43: ## Phase A — non-blocking for everything that is already an fd
44: 
45: | Step | Change | Behaviour change |
46: | --- | --- | --- |
47: | A0 | Return the camera buffer right after the encoder's output DQBUF, instead of at the end of the frame | **yes** — shortens the grab from ~30 ms to ~24 ms |
48: | A1 | Open `camfd` with `O_NONBLOCK`; replace the blocking DQBUF with poll-then-dequeue, handling the `EAGAIN` race | no |
49: | A2 | Give `camenc_ws` an fd-collection API so the main loop can put its listen and client fds into the *same* `pollfd` array, plus a call that services only the ready ones | no |
50: | A3 | Make the loop an explicit state machine (`WAIT` → frame handling → `WAIT`), with the frame-in-flight state introduced now even though A's `QBUF` still blocks | no |
51: | A4 | A `poll()` timeout as a safety net and for periodic housekeeping | no |
52: 
53: **A0 is deliberately separate and separate-testable**: it changes frame timing,
54: so it should not be tangled with a no-behaviour-change refactor.
55: 
56: Expected outcome of A: connections, UI commands and mode-switch requests are
57: prompt (microseconds, independent of frame rate). The only remaining window is
58: the encode.

60: ## Phase B — make the encode wait a poll point
61: 
62: **This is bigger than it first appeared, and it reverses a documented decision.**
63: `rk3576_vepu_codec.c:24-34` says, in the file header:
64: 
65: > A job is encoded synchronously, inside the ioctl that queued it. Nothing needs
66: > a work queue: rk3576_vepu_encode() already waits for the hardware's interrupt,
67: > and the framework calls output_available() from codec_qbuf(), which runs in
68: > task context. … simpler than handing the work to a worker and having to track
69: > a job across two contexts.
70: 
71: **What the difficulty is not.** It is not CPU. The job itself is hardware — the
72: 24 ms is a *wait*, near-zero CPU. The post-job tail costs a cache invalidation
73: over the destination (about 1.9 MB) plus a few pointer operations, so
74: sub-millisecond to a millisecond. Nothing in the encode path is CPU-heavy; the
75: CPU-heavy parts of the pipeline (the demosaic, the copies) are elsewhere.
76: 
77: **What it is.** Cross-context job tracking, and only that. Completion is already
78: the driver's own call — `codec_capture_put_buf()` is a public API invoked by the
79: driver at `rk3576_vepu_codec.c:826`, not something the framework does behind its
80: back. It merely happens to be called inline today, because the driver runs the
81: job synchronously just above it. So no framework change is needed; the driver
82: has to move that tail off the caller's context, which means:
83: 
84: - the in-flight buffers (`cbuf`, `obuf`) and the slice state updated just after
85:   the wait (`gop_index`, `frame_num`, `poc_lsb`, `idr_pic_id`) must live in `priv`
86:   between submission and completion;
87: - a work queue is required for the completion, because it does cache maintenance
88:   and buffer bookkeeping and so cannot run in the interrupt handler;
89: - error reporting moves: today a failed job surfaces in the `QBUF` return value,
90:   and asynchronously it has to surface later, as an event or on `DQBUF`.
91: 
92: That is the whole of it, and it is smaller than it first looked.
93: 
94: | Step | Change |
95: | --- | --- |
96: | B0 | Split `rk3576_vepu_encode()` into submit and wait, both still called synchronously from QBUF. **Semantics-preserving**, and provable: `rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_regs.py` compares the register mirror against MPP, `mutate_check.py` its mutation coverage |
97: | B1 | Carry the job in `priv` and do the tail (`codec_output_put_buf`, the EOS event, `codec_capture_put_buf`) from a work queue on completion, so `QBUF` can return as soon as the hardware has started |
98: | B2 | camenc polls the encoder fd; the state machine carries a frame in flight |
99: | B3 | Re-measure |

101: ### B0 — implemented, verified by the boot selftest

103: `rk3576_vepu_encode()` is now a wrapper over two halves:
104: 
105: | Function | What it is |
106: | --- | --- |
107: | `vepu_start_locked()` | everything up to the write that starts the hardware |
108: | `vepu_wait_locked()` | the wait, the status, the slice FIFO, the reconstruction slot |
109: | `rk3576_vepu_encode()` | validations → take `g_vepu_lock` → start → wait → drop the reference on failure → unlock |
110: 
111: Two things about the shape, both found by reading rather than assumed:
112: 
113: - **`g_vepu_lock` is held across the whole encode**, so it cannot be released
114:   between the halves — the hardware runs one job at a time and the lock is what
115:   says whose it is. In B1 the completion is therefore what releases it.
116: - **The halves share no state.** The working copy of the frame (`job`), the
117:   register base and the start command are all start-side; the interrupt status,
118:   the two lengths and the FIFO's completion flag are all wait-side. `frm`,
119:   `slice` and `result` are the only things that cross, and they are all
120:   arguments. So the split is a cut, not a redesign.

176: 
177: | Framework | `DQBUF` with nothing ready |
178: | --- | --- |
179: | `v4l2_cap` (camera) | waits, unless the fd is `O_NONBLOCK` — which is why camfd has it |
180: | `v4l2_m2m` (encoder) | always `-EAGAIN`; the flag changes nothing |

263:   a poll that returned on a synthetic `POLLERR` produced about 1113.
264: 
265: The one part of the old text that still holds verbatim is its arithmetic: 97 s
266: is about 2900 frames at 30/s and the loop was alive throughout, so it was
267: always a servicing failure and never a frozen loop.
268: 
269: ### What B1 has to do, now that the split exists
270: 
271: `rk3576_vepu_codec.c` currently calls the encoder synchronously from
272: `vepu_service()`, which runs inside the `QBUF` ioctl, and does its own tail
273: inline: `codec_output_put_buf()`, the EOS event, `codec_capture_put_buf()`.
274: B1 is:
275: 
276: - call `vepu_start_locked()`-equivalent from `QBUF` and return, remembering the
277:   in-flight `cbuf`/`obuf` and the slice state that is updated just after the
278:   wait (`gop_index`, `frame_num`, `poc_lsb`, `idr_pic_id`) in `priv`;
279: - run the wait and the tail from a **work queue** on completion — not from the
280:   interrupt handler, which cannot do cache maintenance or touch the buffer
281:   lists;
282: - release `g_vepu_lock` there, and report a failure as an event or on `DQBUF`
283:   rather than through the `QBUF` return value.
284: 
285: 
286: ### What B actually buys, and the alternative
287: 
288: B removes at most ~24 ms of added latency from a connection that arrives during
289: an encode, and turns the encode window into one where the loop can do
290: housekeeping. It is also the natural async boundary for a future SMP. It is
291: **not** a throughput win on one core.
292: 
293: The alternative: **leave the driver alone and give the encode its own thread**
294: (the main loop polls; the thread owns the encoder and signals back). The point
295: of that thread is not to move CPU work — a sleeping thread costs no CPU — but to
296: move the *wait* off the main loop. Same user-visible outcome, no driver risk, at
297: the cost of one thread and a handoff.
298: 
299: Decision (2026-10-05): **phase B is committed, and is not gated on a
300: measurement.**
301: 
302: The reason is not performance. The current version's performance is already
303: sufficient. The conversion is being done for **software-engineering quality**:
304: this is a code sample delivered to other engineers, so the cost of
305: understanding it is part of what is being delivered. A loop that is
306: non-blocking everywhere except one 24 ms hole in the middle is not a smaller
307: thing to read than one that never blocks — it is a larger thing, because the
308: exception has to be found, understood and remembered. B removes the exception.
309: 
310: That reframing supersedes the earlier "measure first, then decide": the
311: measurement would only have settled whether the residual latency mattered,
312: and it does not matter. What matters is that there is no residual.
313: 
314: It also sets the priority for every choice inside the work: **prefer the
315: arrangement a reader gets right the first time over the one that is marginally
316: faster.**
317: 
318: ### Construction order
319: 
320: | Order | Step | Board needed | Why here |
321: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
322: | 1 | A0 — return the camera buffer as soon as the loop is done with it | yes (frame timing changes) | independent, small, and it changes timing, so it must not share a flash with a no-behaviour-change refactor |
323: | 2 | A1–A4 — the loop becomes `poll`-driven, non-blocking DQBUF, `camenc_ws` fds in the same set | yes (regression only) | claims to change no behaviour; verified by comparison |
324: | 3 | B0 — split `rk3576_vepu_encode()` into submit and wait, still called synchronously | **no** | semantics-preserving, provable offline with the register harnesses |
325: | 4 | B1 + B2 — completion moves to a work queue; camenc polls the encoder fd | yes | the two must land together: the driver without the poller leaves the loop blocking in `DQBUF` instead |
326: 
327: ### A0 — verified on the board
328: 
329: The camera's buffer now goes back right after the encoder hands its input
330: container back (`camenc_main.c`, the `camenc_queue(camfd, ...)` call that used to
331: sit at the end of the frame), which is the moment the loop has finished reading
332: it. Before, it was held across the encode, the mux and the emit — most of a frame
333: period, and in the in-place modes that is the encoder's own source buffer, so
334: the capture driver was a buffer short for all of it.
335: 
336: Nothing else moved, and the copied path keeps the same single rule even though
337: it could release even earlier.
338: 
339: Confirmed on the board at 1280x720 (zero-copy active, `encoded where they lie`):
340: 
341: | Reading | Meaning |
342: | --- | --- |
343: | `drops 0 (overrun 0, no buffer 0, stale 0, queue 0)` | the capture driver never wanted for a buffer — the point of the change |
344: | `races 0`, `reading in place` | no tearing; the in-place path still selected |
345: | `97 frames encoded, 0 dropped`, `32.25 steps/s` against `interval 31000 us` | full rate |
346: 
347: The `demosaic … copied 11136 us over 8` in the same dump is the in-place
348: decision's 8-frame sampling period, not a fallback — expected.
349: 
350: **A `-n` frame count is not a duration**: `-n 100` is three seconds of runtime,
351: after which the program exits and the port closes. Worth remembering when a
352: browser "times out" — nothing is listening by then.
353: 
354: ### A1–A4 — implemented, awaiting the board
355: 
356: The loop now sleeps in exactly one place, and it sleeps on everything at once.
357: 
358: | Step | What changed |
359: | --- | --- |
360: | A1 | `camfd` is opened `O_NONBLOCK`; a dequeue with nothing ready answers `EAGAIN`, which `camenc_dequeue()` returns without reporting and the loop reads as "not yet" rather than as a fault |
361: | A2 | `camenc_ws_poll()` is gone. The server now offers its sockets through `camenc_ws_fds()` and acts on the ready ones through `camenc_ws_ready()`, so the camera and the network are waited on by one `poll()` |
362: | A3 | The loop is `for (; i < frames; )` with `i++` at the end of the body: a round that served the server and found no frame has not used a frame number and returns to the same one |
363: | A4 | The wait is bounded by `CAMENC_WAIT_MS` (500 ms) as a safety net for a board where the camera has stopped too — **not** as a polling interval; the camera wakes it 30–60 times a second regardless |
364: 
365: `camenc_wait()` is the whole of it: it fills the array, polls, accounts the wait
366: as the `camera` stage and the service as the `serve` stage, and reports whether
367: the camera has a frame. A source that is not the camera is never waited for —
368: its wait has a zero timeout and only serves the sockets.
369: 
370: Two consequences worth remembering:
371: 
372: - **`camera` in the `us/frame` line still means "time spent waiting"**, which is
373:   what it always measured; the dequeue after it no longer waits, so the figure
374:   stays comparable with earlier runs.
375: - **The `serve` stage now measures the same work as before**, but it happens
376:   when a socket is ready rather than once per frame, so it should be smaller —
377:   and a client that connects during the *inter-frame* wait is answered within
378:   that wait instead of at the end of the frame. The encode window is still not
379:   reachable; that is B.
380: 
381: `camenc_ws_ready()` reads a client for `POLLIN | POLLHUP | POLLERR` and flushes
382: it only for `POLLOUT`, which `camenc_ws_fds()` asks for only when something is
383: queued for that client — a writable socket with nothing to write would wake the
384: loop for nothing.

1: # NuttX network pools, and the two faults they hid
2: 
3: Written after camenc spent days looking like three unrelated application bugs: a
4: `poll()` that reported descriptors nobody could read, clients that could not be
5: let go of when a page was refreshed, and finally a board that could not be
6: connected to at all while its camera ran happily at full rate. There were two
7: causes, both in the board's `defconfig`, both the same shape — **a pool of
8: network structures given a hard ceiling where it wanted a starting size** — and
9: neither one fails in a way that looks like a shortage.
10: 
11: The application's own account of this is at the top of
12: `app/camenc/camenc_ws.c`, which is where someone changing that server will meet
13: it. This file is the RTOS side: what the pools are, what depletes them, and how
14: to tell which one is short.
15: 
16: ## The pools
17: 
18: `MEMPOOL_DEFINE` takes a preallocated count and a dynamic-allocation count. When
19: the second is zero the pool cannot grow: `mempool_allocate()` has no block to
20: hand out, `expandsize` is zero so it cannot ask the heap, and the callers pass a
21: zero timeout so it cannot wait either. It returns `NULL`, and the caller turns
22: that into something else.
23: 
24: | Pool | Prealloc | Dynamic | Depleted by | Failure looks like |
25: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: | `CONFIG_NET_PREALLOC_DEVIF_CALLBACKS` — socket event callbacks | 16 | `CONFIG_NET_ALLOC_DEVIF_CALLBACKS` **was 0** | every connected socket: one connection monitor for its lifetime, one send callback while it has unacknowledged data queued | `tcp_pollsetup()` returns `-EBUSY`; see the amplifier below |
27: | `CONFIG_NET_TCP_PREALLOC_CONNS` — TCP connection structures | 8 | `CONFIG_NET_TCP_ALLOC_CONNS` **was 0** | every connection, held through `TIME_WAIT` after a close this side initiates gently | SYNs dropped in silence |
28: | `CONFIG_NET_UDP_PREALLOC_CONNS` | 8 | `CONFIG_NET_UDP_ALLOC_CONNS` **still 0** | nothing in camenc | — |
29: | `CONFIG_NET_ICMP_PREALLOC_CONNS` | 4 | `CONFIG_NET_ICMP_ALLOC_CONNS` **still 0** | nothing in camenc; but note a leaking user breaks `ping` too | — |
30: 
31: Both `ALLOC` settings are now 1 for the first two. The Kconfig is explicit about
32: what zero means for the connection pool: "Else this will be the maximum number
33: of connections available to the system at all times."
34: 
35: **Raising the ceiling instead was rejected.** `TIME_WAIT` is measured in tens of
36: seconds (`CONFIG_NET_TCP_WAIT_TIMEOUT`) and a browser opens several connections
37: per page load, so any fixed number is a ceiling further away and the failure
38: comes back looking the same. `CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_CONNS` is left at its default,
39: which is no limit.
40: 
41: **Use the value 1, not more.** With 1 a structure is allocated as needed and
42: returned when no longer needed; with 2 or more they are allocated in batches and
43: kept forever.
44: 
45: ## The amplifier: `poll_setup()` abandons the rest of the array
46: 
47: `fs/vfs/fs_poll.c`, in the VFS and not the network stack:
48: 
49: ```c
50:       if (file_poll(fds[i].fd, fds[i].events, &fds[i].revents) < 0)
51:         {
52:           poll_teardown(fds, i, &count);
53:           fds[i].revents |= POLLERR;      /* a condition that has not occurred */
54:           ...
55:           return count + 1;               /* every descriptor after i is dropped */
56:         }
57: ```
58: 
59: Two consequences, and they compound:
60: 
61: 1. `revents` is non-zero, so `poll()` returns immediately and **never waits**.
62:    A loop over several descriptors spins at whatever rate the caller can ask,
63:    and the descriptors after the failing one are never examined or cleared.
64:    camenc puts the listening socket first, so the listener's failure swallowed
65:    every client: `listen (0 in, 1113 err)` beside `client (0 out, 0 err)`.
66: 2. Waiting is the **only** time the per-connection event callbacks are
67:    registered — `tcp_pollsetup()` allocates one and `poll_teardown()` frees it,
68:    and a non-blocking `recv()` neither registers nor waits. So a poll that never
69:    waits is a poll that is never told anything. A reset arrives, `tcp_input()`
70:    sets `TCP_CLOSED` and calls `tcp_callback(TCP_ABORT)`, `tcp_poll_eventhandler()`
71:    would set `s_error` and `POLLERR|POLLHUP` — and none of it happens, because
72:    there is no callback to call. What is left for the application: `recv()`
73:    says `EAGAIN`, `SO_ERROR` says 0, `FIONREAD` says 0.
74: 
75: So one exhausted pool removes the application's only channel for learning that a
76: connection ended, which means the connections that exhausted it are never let go
77: of, which means the pool stays exhausted. A ring, and the reason the first
78: symptoms were so hard to attribute: the server looked like it was simply not
79: trying.
80: 
81: **Also worth knowing:** a registration failure is not necessarily permanent. It
82: depends on the pool's occupancy at that instant, so a connection can sit in the
83: backlog for a long time and then be served. That is the most likely reading of
84: the original 97-second stall in `capture1.pcapng` — the SYN-ACK was sent, the
85: stack answered keepalives promptly throughout, and the application did not
86: `accept()` until a round in which the listener's registration happened to
87: succeed.
88: 
89: ## An independent defect in the read path
90: 
91: Even with the callbacks delivered, half of "the peer has gone" is invisible to a
92: non-blocking reader. `net/tcp/tcp_recvfrom.c`:
93: 
94: - a **FIN** sets `TCP_CLOSE_WAIT` (`tcp_input.c`) and fires `TCP_RXCLOSE`; the
95:   poll callback maps that to `POLLIN` and sets no error, the socket's connected
96:   flag is untouched, and a non-blocking `recv()` on an empty read-ahead returns
97:   `-EAGAIN`;
98: - POSIX requires 0 there — "if no messages are available to be received and the
99:   peer has performed an orderly shutdown, `recv()` shall return 0";
100: - the blocking path is correct (`TCP_RXCLOSE` sets `ir_result = 0`), so only a
101:   non-blocking reader is blind, and a single-threaded server has to be one.
102: 
103: A **RST** does become visible once the callbacks work: the poll callback sets
104: `SO_ERROR`, so `getsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, ...)` confirms it. That is
105: what the `SO_ERROR` check in `camenc_ws_ready()` is for, and it is why a page
106: refresh — which the browser usually closes abortively, because it has unread
107: data — is noticed as soon as `poll()` waits again.
108: 
109: ## Diagnosing which pool is short
110: 
111: The counters that settled it, and what each one rules out:
112: 
113: | Reading | Meaning |
114: | --- | --- |
115: | `rounds` in the thousands per hundred frames | `poll()` is not waiting. It should be about the work: ~100 camera + ~100 encoder per 100 frames |
116: | `listen (N in, M err)` — `err` non-zero, `in` zero | the listener is failing to register, not being selected against |
117: | `client (N out, M err)` | `out` non-zero is the first evidence that the write side is event-driven at all; it was 0 in every window while the callbacks were short |
118: | `rechecks 0`, `idle 0` | the compensations are unreachable, so they can be deleted |
119: | `mem: iob N free` | free IOBs and, in brackets, what a *throttled* transmit allocation may use. Both healthy rules out the buffer pool, which is a different pool from either above and was blamed first, wrongly |
120: | `mem: heap ... free` | what the write-buffer containers and the connection structures come from; 4.2 GB free ruled out heap exhaustion |
121: | `accepted` stuck at 0, no error anywhere, browser says timeout | the connection pool: `tcp_input()` drops the SYN and replies with nothing at all. Grep the log for `No free TCP connections` |
122: | `nerr("ERROR: Failed to allocate callback")` | the callback pool, if `CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES` is on |
123: 
124: Note the asymmetry that cost the most time: the IOB and heap numbers were
125: healthy throughout, because those were not the pools being exhausted.
126: 
127: ## Still upstream, worth reporting
128: 
129: 1. **`poll_setup()` abandoning the descriptors after a failing one.** Anything
130:    that polls several descriptors is exposed. Marking the failing one and
131:    continuing in place of that `return` fixes it.
132: 2. **`tcp_recvfrom.c` returning `EAGAIN` rather than 0 after an orderly close on
133:    a non-blocking socket.** The blocking path is the model.
134: 3. Arguably the default of `CONFIG_NET_ALLOC_DEVIF_CALLBACKS=0` and
135:    `CONFIG_NET_TCP_ALLOC_CONNS=0` in a board config that runs a multi-client
136:    server: the failure mode is not "out of memory" but "the network layer
137:    silently stops telling the application anything".

(End of file - total 137 lines)
</content>
